messages.subject: Re: programmatically creating a Data Frame for Java
messages.subject_clean: programmatically creating a Data Frame for Java
messages.body_plain:
Dear Francesco,

if you think that the documentation can be improved, you can open an issue at https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin-docs/issues. Of course, you can also improve the docs yourself and send us a pull request which we welcome very much!

One remark regarding your first message: a data frame is indeed a compound data type in R and it's essentially a list with special characteristics:
each element has the same length,
the class attribute includes the string "data.frame", and
the attribute row.names exists and is a character or integer vector with length equal to the length of each list element.
So in Renjin you build a (named) list and add the required attributes, which is very much like doing the following in R:

structure(list(a=1, b=2), class = "data.frame", row.names = 1L)

If you don't set the row.names attribute, you will get what looks like a data frame with zero rows but the columns do have:

> structure(list(a=1, b=2), class = "data.frame") -> x
> x
[1] a b
<0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
> str(x)
'data.frame': 0 obs. of  2 variables:
 $ a: num 1
 $ b: num 2

So, indeed, it is required to correctly set the row.names attribute to get a true data frame.

​Regards,

Maarten-Jan

messages.subject: SP package
messages.body_plain:
Dear Renjin community,

The Renjin script engine works like a charm in OrbisGIS and it's pleasure to run R script on PostGIS or H2GIS databases.

We'd like to use the SP package (http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/sp). Is there any plan to support SP in the future ?

By the way, I'm interested to known if some of people in the Renjin community play with spatial geometries (like JTS https://github.com/locationtech/jts).  It seems that JTS could be used to expose geometry from database to R dataframe.

We will be ready to collaborate about this issue.

Best regards

Erwan

Ps : Another colleague  has attempted to experiment the GCC parser to support triangle library (https://github.com/bedatadriven/gcc-bridge-example/issues/2). A major contribution will be about gdal with GCC ;-)

messages.subject: Re: SP package
messages.body_plain:
Hi Erwan,
Great to hear it's going well with OrbisGIS!

I took a quick look at the sp package and it appears that the biggest blockers are remaining limitations in Renjin's implementation of the S4 object system.  Specifically, Renjin doesn't support overridding primitives like [[ or rbind with S4 methods. So you'll see error messages like "object of type 'S4' is not subsettable".

Improving our S4 implementation is one of my own top priorities for the first half of 2017, so I hope that the issues with this package will be resolved at some point this year.

As for integration with JTS, I'm a long time user of JTS as well as geotools, which are fantastic libraries that I would love to see integrated with R/Renjin. I think the challenge there is to find a good balance between harmony with R's existing geospatial APIs like sp, and exploring deeper integration between these libraries and Renjin.

As a starting point, you can take a look at Maarten-Jan's work on an xml2 replacement package that provides an implementation of the API defined in the original xml2 package using Java's built-in XML classes:
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin-xml2

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: Unable to create png using renjin
messages.subject_clean: Unable to create png using renjin
messages.body_plain:
That would be fantastic, PL.

The good news is that the progress we've made with our C to JVM compiler and the GNU R emulation layer should make this a very feasible project, though still non-trivial.

Here's a general overview of how I would approach this:
1. Import C and R sources from the graphics and grDevices package from the latest version of GNU R into the following paths:
packages/graphics/src/main/R
packages/graphics/src/main/c
packages/grDevices/src/main/R
packages/grDevices/src/main/c

You can rip out the sources that are currently there.

2. Update the pom.xml files in graphics and grDevices to include a C compilation step, like packages/stats currently does.
3. At some point, you'll want to rip out the grDevices implementation from GNU R like ps, cairo, png, etc, and replace it with an implementation based on java.awt. This will make it possible to use all the Java imaging libraries to generate png, jpeg, tif, ps, svg, etc.

I don't know exactly what step 3 will look like, but my sense is that grDevices have a relatively small API to implement.

If you get started with steps 1 and 2 and open a pull request, I can help point you in the right direction from there.

Best,
Alex

messages.body_plain:
Hi PL,
We are also developing on Ubuntu 16 so that's a good choice!

Have you seen the building instructions here:
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/blob/master/BUILDING.md

On Ubuntu, should be able to install all the required tools using:

sudo apt-get install openjdk-7-jdk maven make gcc-4.7 gcc-4.7-plugin-dev gfortran-4.7 g++-4.7 gcc-4.7.multilib g++-4.7-multilib
If you are still having fortran problems, post error message and the output from "gfortran-4.7 -v" to a gist and share the link here.

Best,
Alex
